title: Physics front-end vs plain Kerr MLP across widths
question: Does the physical part pay off at every width or only at small ones (E020: hybrid h48 cm30 67.6 % vs class a 66.0 %, 3 vs 5 seeds)?
git_commit: recorded per run in results/runs/*.json (field git_commit); rule commit: see LOG.md
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
recipe_rule: recipe of the E025 pair with the nearest width on a log scale (F2/F9 at h48)
hybrid: PhysPlusMLP: PhysKerr(R, L, sym) + one-hidden Kerr MLP in parallel, joint (E017/E020)

rule_draft.status: DRAFT: to be confirmed by the user before the first run; must not change after results are seen
rule_draft.pays_off: the front-end pays off at width h if hybrid - pure >= 1 p.p. (5 seeds, intervals do not overlap)
rule_draft.decreasing: the gain decreases with h if the difference at h = 16 exceeds that at h = 119 by >= 1 p.p.
rule_draft.thesis: a gain only at small h is the thesis 'physics saves multiplies'
rule_draft.noise: thresholds in p.p. are compared with results/noise_floor.json (E024): MDD(5 seeds) = t_{0.975,8} * s_pooled * sqrt(2/5); 0.1 dB of Q2 = 6 p.p. at 10 %, 4.1 at 48 %, 3.0 at 66 %, 2.7 at 70 % (anchors); every table prints both
